takeaway: Acral lentiginous melanoma is more common in darker-skinned people, on palms, soles and mucous membranes. Superficial spreading is the commonest overall; lentigo maligna is on the elderly face.

question.text: Which of the following subtypes of malignant melanoma is more common in darker-skinned individuals?
question.say: Which of the following subtypes of malignant melanoma is more common in darker-skinned individuals?

lines.text: Five subtypes of malignant melanoma are recognised. Here a child with darker skin shows a dark patch on the palm and the sole.
The little hiker leaves a dark trail across the palm and sole. That is acral lentiginous melanoma, more common in darker-skinned people.
It is found mostly on the palms, soles and mucous membranes.
Lentigo maligna is commonly found on the face of elderly patients, so it is crossed out.
Superficial spreading is the most common subtype overall, mostly on the lower limb or trunk.
Nodular is the round lump, also crossed out here.
So the answer is acral lentiginous melanoma.
